title: The Four-Hand Duet  (El dúo a cuatro manos)

segments.t: La luz dorada de la tarde entra sesgada por los postigos verdes abiertos de la habitación nueve mientras Evelyn y Caleb terminan los animados compases finales de su dúo de piano a cuatro manos y Hannah escucha junto a la puerta. Escucha primero toda la escena.
Softly into the bridge now, Caleb... let the bass notes walk like gentle footsteps.
Breathing first, answering second — right up to middle D together!
Look out under the shade tree: not a single teacup is clinking anywhere!
Here comes our bright final scale to the top — one, two, three, and hold!
BRAVO! Listen to all twenty-eight chairs clapping across the courtyard stones!
Evelyn, I did not rush bar sixteen — and I forgot all about counting meters!
You played like a true musician, Caleb, and look who is standing up at table one!
Your old professor is lifting his teacup high toward the sunroom window!
And he is waving Hannah and Arthur over to open that brown paper parcel!
Go on out under the lanterns, both of you — I am right behind you.
Here is the ivory toast card he asked us to read to the courtyard!
Thirty summers between two songs — and the courtyard sounds warmer than ever.
Repasemos ahora, compás a compás, este gran momento musical.
Softly into the bridge now, Caleb... let the bass notes walk like gentle footsteps.
'Suavemente hacia el puente, Caleb... deja que las notas graves caminen como pasos tranquilos.' Softly es «suavemente, con poco volumen», e into the bridge marca la entrada en esa parte de la pieza:
Softly into the bridge now, Caleb
con let + objeto + verbo base, «deja que...»:
let the bass notes walk like gentle footsteps
Breathing first, answering second — right up to middle D together!
'¡Primero respirar, después responder: hasta el re central, juntos!' Las formas -ing breathing y answering funcionan aquí como sustantivos, igual que nuestros infinitivos:
Breathing first, answering second
y right up to significa «justo hasta arriba»:
right up to middle D together
Look out under the shade tree: not a single teacup is clinking anywhere!
'Miren bajo el árbol de sombra: ¡ni una sola taza tintinea en ningún sitio!' Look out significa aquí «mirar hacia fuera», y clink es el tintineo del cristal o la loza:
Look out under the shade tree
con not a single, «ni un solo», al principio de la oración:
not a single teacup is clinking anywhere
Here comes our bright final scale to the top — one, two, three, and hold!
'Aquí llega nuestra brillante escala final hasta arriba: un, dos, tres, ¡y aguantamos!' Scale es la «escala» musical, y here comes anuncia algo que llega:
Here comes our bright final scale to the top
y hold, en música, es «sostener» la nota:
one, two, three, and hold
BRAVO! Listen to all twenty-eight chairs clapping across the courtyard stones!
'¡BRAVO! ¡Escuchen las veintiocho sillas aplaudiendo de un lado a otro de las losas del patio!' Clap es «aplaudir» y across significa «de un lado a otro de»:
Listen to all twenty-eight chairs clapping
una metonimia graciosa: las sillas aplauden por la gente sentada en ellas:
across the courtyard stones
Evelyn, I did not rush bar sixteen — and I forgot all about counting meters!
'Evelyn, no me aceleré en el compás dieciséis, ¡y me olvidé por completo de contar metros!' Rush bar sixteen, sin preposición, es «precipitar el compás dieciséis»:
I did not rush bar sixteen
y forget all about es «olvidarse por completo de»:
I forgot all about counting meters
You played like a true musician, Caleb, and look who is standing up at table one!
'Tocaste como un auténtico músico, Caleb, ¡y mira quién se está poniendo de pie en la mesa uno!' Like + sustantivo significa «como»; true musician es «un auténtico músico»:
You played like a true musician, Caleb
y stand up es «ponerse de pie»:
look who is standing up at table one
Your old professor is lifting his teacup high toward the sunroom window!
'¡Tu antiguo profesor levanta bien alto su taza hacia la ventana de la galería!' Lift es «levantar» y high, detrás del objeto, significa «bien alto»:
Your old professor is lifting his teacup high
y sunroom es una galería acristalada para tomar el sol:
toward the sunroom window
And he is waving Hannah and Arthur over to open that brown paper parcel!
'¡Y le hace señas a Hannah y a Arthur para que vayan a abrir ese paquete de papel marrón!' Wave someone over es «hacer señas a alguien para que se acerque»:
he is waving Hannah and Arthur over
con to + verbo para la finalidad:
to open that brown paper parcel
Go on out under the lanterns, both of you — I am right behind you.
'Salgan bajo los farolillos, los dos; yo voy justo detrás de ustedes.' Go on out combina dos partículas: on anima a seguir y out indica «hacia fuera»:
Go on out under the lanterns, both of you
y right behind you es «justo detrás de ti»:
I am right behind you
Here is the ivory toast card he asked us to read to the courtyard!
'¡Aquí está la tarjeta color marfil con el brindis que nos pidió leer al patio!' Ivory es «marfil», como color, y ask someone to + verbo es «pedir a alguien que haga algo»:
Here is the ivory toast card
en una oración de relativo sin that:
he asked us to read to the courtyard
Thirty summers between two songs — and the courtyard sounds warmer than ever.
'Treinta veranos entre dos canciones, y el patio suena más cálido que nunca.' Between sitúa algo «entre» dos elementos, y warmer than ever es «más cálido que nunca»:
Thirty summers between two songs
con sound + adjetivo, «sonar»:
the courtyard sounds warmer than ever
Escuchemos de nuevo toda la escena, a ritmo natural.
Softly into the bridge now, Caleb... let the bass notes walk like gentle footsteps.
Breathing first, answering second — right up to middle D together!
Look out under the shade tree: not a single teacup is clinking anywhere!
Here comes our bright final scale to the top — one, two, three, and hold!
BRAVO! Listen to all twenty-eight chairs clapping across the courtyard stones!
Evelyn, I did not rush bar sixteen — and I forgot all about counting meters!
You played like a true musician, Caleb, and look who is standing up at table one!
Your old professor is lifting his teacup high toward the sunroom window!
And he is waving Hannah and Arthur over to open that brown paper parcel!
Go on out under the lanterns, both of you — I am right behind you.
Here is the ivory toast card he asked us to read to the courtyard!
Thirty summers between two songs — and the courtyard sounds warmer than ever.
Cuatro manos en un piano rescatado ponen en pie a todo el patio, y ahora el paquete plano marrón espera bajo el árbol. Nos vemos en la próxima escena.
See you soon!
